Color Organisms

2014
Generative software, video, 5:37

Color Organisms is an experiment in artificial life that begins with a random assortment of colored organisms. As they age and grow, they become able to mate under a few simple rules: an organism that has reached maturity (about twelve seconds), hasn’t mated in the last four seconds, and finds a nearby partner at least 10% different in hue produces a child whose hue lies exactly between its parents’ on the color wheel. Organisms die of old age, but with nothing else to check it, the population grows exponentially. The result is a shifting, unpredictable composition of pure color, every moment of it determined by the rules.
